description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace_check" to hold intermediate artifacts and results.  
2. Recursively enumerate all filesystem entries under /working and save the full paths to "temp_workspace_check/all_paths.txt".  
3. From "all_paths.txt", extract entries whose basename is exactly "workspace" and save those paths to "temp_workspace_check/matching_paths.txt".  
4. For each path listed in "matching_paths.txt", retrieve and record file metadata (type, permissions, and any link target) into "temp_workspace_check/matching_metadata.txt".  
5. From "matching_metadata.txt", filter and save only the entries identified as regular files to "temp_workspace_check/regular_files.txt".  
6. Count the number of lines in "regular_files.txt" and write that numeric count to "temp_workspace_check/regular_count.txt".  
7. Check for and record any unexpected cases (such as symbolic links or directories named "workspace") into "temp_workspace_check/discrepancies.txt" for later review.  
8. Prune "all_paths.txt" of entries unrelated to the basename "workspace", consolidate the remaining artifacts, and save a compact manifest to "temp_workspace_check/compact_manifest.txt".  
9. Create a marker file "temp_workspace_check/result_ready.txt" that references "regular_count.txt" and indicates readiness to produce the final decision (produce "yes" if the count is greater than zero, otherwise "no") without emitting the decision itself.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme

description:
1. Create a temporary directory named "temp_workspace" to hold intermediate files and logs.  
2. Capture a full recursive listing of the filesystem tree rooted at /working and save it to "temp_workspace/tree_snapshot.txt".  
3. From that snapshot, extract all entries whose basename is exactly "workspace" and save them to "temp_workspace/candidate_entries.txt".  
4. For each candidate entry, determine its filesystem type and record entries as "path -> type" in "temp_workspace/entry_types.txt".  
5. Remove any lines in "temp_workspace/entry_types.txt" that denote directories, symbolic links, or special files, leaving only regular-file entries.  
6. De-duplicate the remaining paths and save the result to "temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt".  
7. Verify that each path in "temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt" resides under /working and is accessible, recording any inaccessible paths to "temp_workspace/inaccessible.txt".  
8. If any inaccessible paths were found, log a warning and remove those paths from "temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt", appending actions to "temp_workspace/cleanup.log".  
9. Prepare a final check that will read "temp_workspace/unique_workspace_files.txt" and determine whether to output "yes" if it contains at least one accessible regular file named "workspace", or "no" if it is empty.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && mkdir /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace_check" to hold all intermediate results and ensure it is empty before proceeding.  
2. Obtain a recursive listing of the /working hierarchy and save the raw listing to "temp_workspace_check/recursive_listing.txt".  
3. From the raw listing, extract every path whose final component is exactly "workspace" and save those paths to "temp_workspace_check/candidate_paths.txt".  
4. For each path in candidate_paths.txt, retrieve and record its filesystem metadata (including type information) into "temp_workspace_check/candidate_metadata.txt".  
5. Filter candidate_metadata.txt to produce "temp_workspace_check/regular_candidates.txt" containing only entries identified as regular files.  
6. Deduplicate regular_candidates.txt, produce "temp_workspace_check/regular_unique.txt" with canonical paths, and write the number of unique entries to "temp_workspace_check/regular_count.txt".  
7. Perform a consistency verification that each canonical path resides under /working and that metadata matches the recorded type, writing any discrepancies to "temp_workspace_check/consistency_report.txt".  
8. Archive the intermediate artifacts (recursive_listing.txt, candidate_paths.txt, candidate_metadata.txt, regular_candidates.txt, regular_unique.txt, regular_count.txt, consistency_report.txt) into "temp_workspace_check/workspace_check_archive" and remove transient temp files while retaining the canonical files and reports.  
9. Create a control file "temp_workspace_check/final_prep.txt" summarizing the canonical regular path list, the verified count, and pointers to the archive and consistency report, preparing the state for the final decision step.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace_checks" to hold all intermediate artifacts for this procedure.  
2. Capture and save a current snapshot of /working (its top-level metadata) into "temp_workspace_checks/original_state.txt".  
3. Produce a full recursive listing of /working and save the raw listing to "temp_workspace_checks/raw_listing.txt".  
4. From the raw listing, extract every entry whose filename is exactly "workspace" and save those candidate paths to "temp_workspace_checks/matches_candidates.txt".  
5. For each candidate path, collect filesystem metadata (type, size, permissions, owner) and append results to "temp_workspace_checks/type_checks.txt".  
6. Normalize and deduplicate the candidate paths from the type checks, writing the unique resolved path list to "temp_workspace_checks/unique_candidates.txt".  
7. For each unique candidate, resolve any references (such as links) and record the final target path and its resolved metadata to "temp_workspace_checks/resolved_candidates.txt".  
8. Produce a concise summary that notes which resolved targets are regular files and record this per-path verdict into "temp_workspace_checks/summary.txt", including any permission or access errors encountered.  
9. Load "temp_workspace_checks/summary.txt", set a decision placeholder that maps the presence of any regular-file verdict to a single-line result, and prepare to emit that single-line result while leaving all intermediate artifacts intact for audit.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/workspace
